summary: Matthew Immergut works in religious studies and related fields. A student of Culadasa, he was an Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York, attested in 2011.

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto by 2014 under Frances Garrett, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, the University of Hawaiʻi (MA), and Duke University (PhD, attested 2015) under Richard M. Jaffe.

Matthew T. Kapstein is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at Brown University (1987). His posts include Columbia University (~1989–1996), University of Chicago (1986–1998), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2002).
Matthias de Vries was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1838–1843). He later held posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer was a linguist who studied at Graz and Erlangen-Nürnberg (PhD ~1859–1860). He held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1864–1868), University of Würzburg (from 1868), and University of Munich (from 1890).

Matthieu Ricard is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy figure. He earned a doctorate in molecular biology at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob (~1967–1972) and studied under traditional teachers Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse.

Mattia Salvini specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~2005–2011) under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University (attested 2015).

Mauli Chand Prasad specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson was an Indology specialist who served as the South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago, attested in 1984 and 2007.

Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins (PhD ~1878–1879), studying under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He served as professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1888–1892) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He subsequently held a post at the University of Montpellier from around 1895 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel specialized in sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École des Langues Orientales from ~1875 to 1879, where he later held an academic post from ~1886 to 1889.
Maurice O'Connell Walshe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the University of London from ~1955 to 1978.

Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar educated at Christ's College and Ridley Hall. He held posts at Ridley Hall, University of Ibadan, Clare College, and King's College London, before serving as Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford (1970–1991).

Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba, under Nadia Boulanger, and with Buddhist teachers Yasutani, Shimano, and Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Mauro Maggi completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Naples "L'Orientale." He held posts at the University of Hamburg (1990), Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente, the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, and the University of Rome.

Mavis L. Fenn studied at the universities of Winnipeg, Calgary, and McMaster (PhD attested 1994, under Graeme MacQueen). She held posts at St. Paul's University College (2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016) in religious and Asian studies.

Max Deeg completed his Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of School of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University, attested between 2010 and 2021.
